title: The Man Who Sold the Eiffel Tower
sources: Smithsonian Magazine, 'The Smoothest Con Man That Ever Lived' (1925: newspaper story on the tower's rust and upkeep costs; forged government stationery; private meetings at the Hotel de Crillon; dealer Andre Poisson paid and never reported it; Lustig returned to try again, then fled to the United States)

Also read for cross-checking: France Today, 'How the Eiffel Tower Was Sold'; The Hustle, 'The con man who sold the Eiffel Tower, twice'; ISRI, 'Selling the Eiffel Tower'. Exact sums and dealer counts differ between sources, so the script leaves them out.

lines.text: In nineteen twenty-five, a con man sold the Eiffel Tower.
lines.caps: in *nineteen twenty-five, | a *con man | *sold the | eiffel *tower

lines.text: See, he'd read that the tower was rusting,
and that Paris was paying a fortune to fix it,
lines.caps: and *paris was | paying a *fortune | to *fix it

lines.text: so he sent forged letters to scrap dealers, pretending to be a government official.
lines.caps: so he sent | *forged letters | to *scrap dealers | pretending to be | a *government official

lines.text: He invited them to a private meeting at a fancy hotel,
lines.caps: he *invited them | to a *private meeting | at a *fancy hotel

lines.text: where one nervous dealer handed over a suitcase of cash.
lines.caps: where one | *nervous dealer | handed over | a *suitcase of cash

lines.text: and the dealer was too embarrassed to call the police.
lines.caps: and the *dealer | too *embarrassed | to call the *police

lines.text: So he came back and tried it again,
lines.caps: so he *came back | and *tried it again

lines.text: but this time he got spooked, and fled to America.
lines.caps: but this time | he got *spooked | and fled to *america

lines.text: And yes, the tower is still standing.
